Q: Richtextbox crashes Excel if a Ctrl-C (copy) or a drag and drop is attempted A:

My hint;

step one - open cmd with open cmd with administrator privileges - type regsvr32 richtx32.ocx

step two - Find your UserForm delete code; and past this code;

Option Explicit

Private Sub UserForm_Initialize()
    Me.KeyPreview = True
    RichTextBox1.OLEDragMode = 0
    RichTextBox1.OLEDropMode = 0
End Sub

Private Sub UserForm_KeyDown(ByVal KeyCode As MSForms.ReturnInteger, ByVal Shift As Integer)
    If Shift = 2 Then
        Select Case KeyCode
            Case vbKeyC
                If RichTextBox1.SelLength > 0 Then
                    SetClipboardText RichTextBox1.SelText
                    KeyCode = 0
                End If
            Case vbKeyX
                If RichTextBox1.SelLength > 0 Then
                    SetClipboardText RichTextBox1.SelText
                    RichTextBox1.SelText = ""
                    KeyCode = 0
                End If
            Case vbKeyV
                If ClipboardHasText() Then
                    RichTextBox1.SelText = GetClipboardText()
                    KeyCode = 0
                End If
        End Select
    End If
End Sub

Private Function ClipboardHasText() As Boolean
    Dim clip As MSForms.DataObject
    Set clip = New MSForms.DataObject
    clip.GetFromClipboard
    ClipboardHasText = clip.GetFormat(1)
End Function

Private Function GetClipboardText() As String
    Dim clip As MSForms.DataObject
    Set clip = New MSForms.DataObject
    clip.GetFromClipboard
    If clip.GetFormat(1) Then GetClipboardText = clip.GetText
End Function

Private Sub SetClipboardText(ByVal text As String)
    Dim clip As MSForms.DataObject
    Set clip = New MSForms.DataObject
    clip.SetText text
    clip.PutInClipboard
End Sub

Important: if your RichTextBox control has a different name (like RichTextBox2), replace every occurrence of RichTextBox1 in the code above with the exact name of your control.

step three - copy in one module this code, delete what you had put;

Sub RTBX()
    UserForm1.Show 0
End Sub

Save and test;

Close the VBA editor.
Save the file as file (.xlsm).
Run the RTBX macro (from Alt+F8, or by assigning it to a button).
Type something in the RichTextBox, then try Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, or dragging the text.

Finally, if you find any errors in your code, please let us know the error, or post your userform code and You need to enable the Microsoft Forms 2.0 Object Library in the VBA references (Tools > References) for the UserForm to work properly.

Q: `lubridate::floor_date` returns inaccurate values (just below the actual rounding unit) A:

Here is a function which stitches a string with the exact milliseconds:

convert_timestamp_to_ms_character <- function(ts) {
  # timestamp string in seconds
  ts_char <- strftime(ts, format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS0")

  # milliseconds
  ts_ms_char <- as.character(floor(unclass(ts)*1000))
  l <- nchar(ts_ms_char)
  ms <- substr(ts_ms_char, start = l-2, stop = l)

  # timezone
  tz <- format(ts, format = "%Z")

  return(paste0(c(ts_char, ".", ms, " ", tz), collapse = ""))
}

# testing:
convert_timestamp_to_ms_character(as.POSIXct("1970-01-01 12:00:00.000", tz = "Europe/London"))
convert_timestamp_to_ms_character(as.POSIXct("1970-01-01 12:00:00.001", tz = "Europe/London"))
convert_timestamp_to_ms_character(as.POSIXct("1970-01-01 12:00:00.002", tz = "Europe/London"))
convert_timestamp_to_ms_character(as.POSIXct("1970-01-01 12:00:00.999999", tz = "Europe/London"))
for (i in seq_len(100)) {
  print(convert_timestamp_to_ms_character(Sys.time()))
}

Note that the output is of class character, it just looks like a timestamp. However, this serves its purpose regarding exporting to my database.

if it's not Pair, Triple, a tuple, or a finite set of things (ARGB tuple for color) then it's most likely just not destructuable in a reasonable manner. I've seen ("data, callback") be destructured but even that was not valid.

Q: How to stop Google sheet from auto convert dates to numbers? A:

I don't think its possible to change the automatic behavior, however, based in the official documentation as a workaround you can use the API to send a batch update to change the cell format to Date.

For this you would need to use the API method spreadsheets.batchUpdate and include a UpdateCells request. What you are looking to modify in the request is the NumberFormatType parameter and set the value to DATE in order to change the format.

References:

  • Method: spreadsheets.batchUpdate
  • UpdateCells
  • NumberFormatType

Q: Azure Data factory - data flow expression date and timestamp conversions A:

  1. toDate() converts input date string to date with default format as yyyy-[M]M-[d]d. Accepted formats are :[ yyyy, yyyy-[M]M, yyyy-[M]M-[d]d, yyyy-[M]M-[d]dT* ].

    Same goes with toTimestamp(), the default pattern is yyyy-[M]M-[d]d hh:mm:ss[.f...] when it is used.

  2. In Azure SQL Database as well the default date and datetime2 formats are in YYYY-MM-DD and YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss as shown below.

  1. But if your column datatypes are in string (varchar) format, then you can change the output format of date and DateTime in azure data flow mappings.

When loaded to Azure SQL database, it is shown as below:

Note: This format results when datatype is varchar

  1. If the datatype is the date in the Azure SQL database, you can convert them to the required format using date conversions as

select id, col1, date1, convert(varchar(10),date1,105) as 'dd-MM-YYYY' from test1

  1. Azure SQL Database always follows the UTC time zone. Using “AT TIME ZONE” convert it another non-UTC time zone.

select getdate() as a, getdate() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AT TIME ZONE 'Central Standard Time' as b

You can also refer to sys.time_zone_info view to check current UTC offset information.

select * from sys.time_zone_info
